the development of a new method for the catalytic and stereodivergent glycosylation with glycosyl fluorides by using various protic acids as the catalysts.
the development of a new catalytic and stereospecific glycosylation with a glycosyl fluoride by using various protic acids as a catalyst.

the glycosylation of glucosyl fluoride with various glycosyl acceptors was effectively catalyzed by using various protic acids such as HClO4, B(C6F 5)4, H2SO4, HBF4·OEt2, and HCl.

the glycosylation with a glycosyl fluoride was effectively promoted by a protic acid catalyst and that the stereocontrol of glycosidation was achieved by a combination of the catalyst and solvent.

the glycosylation with glycosyl fluoride was performed with a catalytic amount (1.0–10.0 equiv) of protic acids such as perchloric acid, p-toluenesulfonic acid, trifluoromethanesulfonic acid, and trifluoroacetic acid, in a mixed solvent such as Et2O, CH2Cl2, or BTF–tBuCN = (5: 1).

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of protic acids as a catalyst in glycosylation reactions is an effective and practical method for the stereoselective synthesis of glycosides.
a variety of glycosides can be prepared with a catalytic amount (0.05–0.1 equiv) of a protic acid in the presence of Et2O or BTF–tBuCN (5:1) as the solvent.
protic acids, which are generally regarded as poor glycosyl donors, can be used to generate glycosyl fluorides in situ and promote the glycosylation reaction.
